validity.researcher_notes: Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod is a real line. The European Investment Bank project page, English Wikipedia and Offshore Technology all describe it, so existence is settled and it is correctly a transmission trunk. It is not a duplicate: P0774 Progress and P0761 Soyuz run in the same corridor but are separate strings. Length 4,451 km matches Offshore Technology exactly, and English Wikipedia says about 4,500 km. Capacity 32 bcm/y matches English Wikipedia. Commissioning is 1984 in English Wikipedia and Offshore Technology, while the sheet says 1983, so a one year difference. The second diameter figure, 1400 mm, is not in any page found. Owner1 100 percent for Gazprom beside the Ukrainian operator conflicts with sources that name both as owners.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Cannot tell. Russian transit through Ukraine ended on 1 January 2025 when the agreement between the Ukrainian operator and Gazprom expired. Ukraine imported 6.5 bcm of gas in 2025, mostly from Hungary and Poland, so the Ukrainian system is in use, but no page found names this line as carrying that gas. English Wikipedia says Russia stopped exporting through this line at the end of 2024. The European Investment Bank page describes rehabilitation of the Ukrainian section in earlier years. Whether the Ukrainian section still carries domestic or reverse flow is not stated for this line, so the status is left as operating and flagged for a person to decide between operating and idle. This covers the Ukrainian section. The Russian section has been unused for transit since 2025.
